Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Learned A.G.A. has informed that notice to the informant has been served on 7.7.2024.
2.

Compliance affidavit of Sri Arman Ahmad, presently posted as Sub-Inspector at Police Station
Madhuban Bapudham, District Ghaziabad is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Anand Pati Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Pranshu Kumar,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.16 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Madhuban Bapudham, District- Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
5.The applicant is stated to be the tenant of the informant earlier on and had befriended the daughter of the informant, as such he was expelled from the house.
The applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant on 14.1.2024 at about 02:00 a.m.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7.
The victim is major and in her own statement also recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has stated her age to be 17 years.
The school certificate of the victim is forged one and cannot be relied as it is of class XIth, which indicates her date of birth to be 1.1.2010.

Reliance has been placed on the judgment of the Supreme Court in P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525, whereby it has been observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim,
no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.

entities.text: P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., whereby it is stated that she out of her own sweet-will had gone with the applicant to Patna and remained there for about fifteen days and returned only when the money got exhausted.
9.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
10. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 29.1.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)
11.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
12. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

2 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
13. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.

14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Deepak involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
16.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

17. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
